text:
Long ago, a rich and prosperous kingdom was ruled by a king named Mansur. He was a just and wise ruler, but near the end of his life, one heavy thought gave him no peace: he had no children. Who would inherit the throne?

One day the king summoned his trusted vizier and said, “I want to leave the throne to an honest person with a pure heart. Gather all the children of the kingdom at the palace.”

The next day, hundreds of children gathered in the palace square. There were sons of rich men and children of the poor. The king looked at them and said:

“My children, I will give each of you one seed. Plant it at home, in a flowerpot, and care for it for one year. After a year, each of you will bring your flower to the palace. Whoever has the most beautiful flower will become my heir.”

The children rejoiced, took their seeds, and scattered. Among them was a boy named Sardor. He lived in a poor hut, but he had a clear heart and was hardworking. Arriving home, Sardor found the best soil, filled a pot, planted the seed, and watered it every day.

A week passed, and nothing came up. Two weeks, three weeks. In the other children’s pots, shoots were turning green and flowers were beginning to bloom. But in Sardor’s pot, there was still only bare soil.

“Why?” Sardor wondered. He changed the soil, added fertilizer, put the pot in the sun, then in the shade. At night he stayed awake watching it. But the seed did not grow.

Months passed. The neighboring children boasted: “My flower is red, big, and fragrant!” “Mine is even more beautiful!” Sardor stayed silent, eyes on the ground, ashamed.

After a year, the king announced the day. All the children set off for the palace with magnificent flowers. In their hands were the most beautiful, colorful, rare blooms.

Sardor decided to go too. His mother said, “Son, why are you going with an empty pot? People will laugh.” Sardor replied, “Mother, I did everything I could. I planted the seed the king gave me honestly. I’ll show the empty pot honestly too.”

The palace square was filled with flowers. Every child held their flower high. The king, dressed simply, walked slowly among the children and looked at the flowers. He didn’t say a word, and he didn’t smile once.

At last he noticed Sardor standing off to the side with his head lowered. The boy was clutching an empty pot, and there were tears in his eyes.

“Who are you, boy?” asked the king. “Why is your pot empty?”

Sardor answered with a trembling voice: “Your Majesty, I planted the seed, watered it every day, and did everything I could. But it didn’t sprout. I have no flower, but I don’t want to deceive myself. So I brought the truth.”

The king fell silent. Then he announced loudly across the whole square:

“Here is my heir!”

Everyone froze in astonishment. “How?” they whispered. “With an empty pot?”

The king said, “A year ago, every seed I gave you had been boiled beforehand. Not one of them could have sprouted. Not one. No flower could have grown from the seeds you planted.”

Silence fell over the square.

“That means the flowers in your hands were grown from other seeds,” the king continued. “But this boy did not buy his success or cheat. He came with an empty pot but a clear conscience. I need someone to rule this kingdom. Someone honest, who admits his mistakes and is not afraid of the truth.”

Sardor couldn’t believe his ears. The other children lowered their heads in shame.

And so, years later, Sardor became a just and beloved king. He always said, “Honesty with empty hands is worth more than fake wealth.”

Moral: Honesty doesn’t always bring profit, but it is always right. A victory won by deceit will be exposed sooner or later, while an honest defeat makes you great. Never be afraid to tell the truth.

tr.title: Podshoh va urug’lar
paragraphs: Qadim zamonda, boy va obod bir mamlakatni Mansur ismli podshoh boshqarar ekan. U adolatli va dono hukmdor ekan, lekin umrining oxirlariga kelib, bitta og’ir o’y uni tinch qo’ymas ekan: uning farzandi yo’q ekan. Taxtni kimga qoldirish kerak?
Bir kuni podshoh o’ziga yaqin vazirini chaqirib debdi: «Men taxtni halol va pok yurakli odamga qoldirmoqchiman. Mamlakatdagi barcha yosh bolalarni saroyga to’plang.»
Ertasiga saroy maydoniga yuzlab bola yig’ilibdi. Ular ichida boylarning o’g’illari ham, kambag’allarning bolalari ham bor ekan. Podshoh ularga qarab debdi:

«Bolalarim, men sizlarga bittadan urug’ beraman. Uni o’z uyingizda, o’zingiz gul tuvagiga ekasiz va bir yil parvarish qilasiz. Bir yildan keyin hammangiz gulingizni saroyga olib kelasiz. Kimning guli eng chiroyli bo’lsa, o’sha mening vorisim bo’ladi.»

Bolalar quvonib, urug’larni olib tarqalishibdi. Ular orasida Sardor ismli bola ham bor ekan. U kambag’al kulbada yashar, lekin yuragi tiniq va mehnatsevar bola ekan. Sardor uyiga yetib, eng yaxshi tuproqni topibdi, tuvakka solib, urug’ni ekibdi va har kuni sug’orib turibdi.

Bir hafta o’tibdi, hech narsa chiqmabdi. Ikki hafta, uch hafta o’tibdi. Boshqa bolalarning tuvaklarida novdalar ko’karib, gullar ochila boshlabdi. Sardorning tuvagida esa hamon bo’m-bo’sh tuproq turar ekan.
«Nima uchun?» deb o’ylabdi Sardor. U tuproqni almashtiribdi, o’g’it solibdi, quyoshga qo’yibdi, soyaga olibdi. Kechalari uxlamay, tuvakni kuzatibdi. Lekin urug’ o’smabdi.
Oylar o’tibdi. Qo’shni bolalar maqtanib yurar ekan: «Mening gulim qizil, katta va xushbo’y!» «Meniki undan ham chiroyli!» Sardor esa jim yurar, ko’zlarini yerga tikib, xijolat chekar ekan.
Bir yil o’tib, podshoh belgilangan kunni e’lon qilibdi. Barcha bolalar ajoyib gullar bilan saroyga yo’l olibdi. Ularning qo’lida eng chiroyli, rang-barang, noyob gullar bor ekan.

Sardor ham borishga qaror qilibdi. Onasi unga debdi: «O’g’lim, nega bo’sh tuvak bilan borasan? Odamlar kulishadi.» Sardor esa javob beribdi: «Onajon, men bor kuchimni sarfladim. Podshoh bergan urug’ni halollik bilan ekdim. Bo’sh tuvakni ham halol ko’rsataman.»

Saroy maydoni gullarga to’lib ketgan ekan. Hamma bola o’z gulini baland ko’tarib turgan ekan. Podshoh oddiy kiyimda, bolalar orasidan sekin yurib chiqibdi va gullarga ko’z tashlabdi. U na bir so’z demabdi, na bir tabassum qilibdi.
Oxirida u bir chetda, boshini egib turgan Sardorni ko’ribdi. U bo’sh tuvakni mahkam ushlab turar ekan, ko’zlarida yosh bor ekan.
«Bola, sen kimsan?» deb so’rabdi podshoh. «Nima uchun tuvaging bo’sh?»

Sardor titrab javob beribdi: «Podshohim, men urug’ni ekdim, har kuni sug’ordim, hamma narsani qildim. Lekin u o’smadi. Menda gul yo’q, lekin o’zimni aldamoqchi emasman. Shuning uchun haqiqatni olib keldim.»
Podshoh jim qolibdi. Keyin ovozini ko’tarib, butun maydonga e’lon qilibdi:
«Mana mening vorisim!»
Hamma hayratdan qotib qolibdi. «Qanday?» deb pichirlashibdi. «Bo’sh tuvak bilan?»

Podshoh debdi: «Bir yil oldin men sizlarga bergan urug’larning hammasini oldindan qaynatib, pishirib bergan edim. Ularning hech biri o’sa olmasdi. Hech biri. Sizlar ekkan urug’lardan gul chiqishi mumkin emas edi.»
Maydonda jimlik cho’kibdi.

«Demak, sizlar qo’lingizdagi gullarni boshqa urug’dan o’stirgansizlar», deb davom etibdi podshoh. «Bu bola esa o’z yutug’ini sotib olish yoki aldash o’rniga, bo’sh tuvak bilan, lekin sof vijdon bilan keldi. Menga mamlakatni boshqaradigan odam kerak. Halol, o’z xatosini tan oladigan va haqiqatdan qo’rqmaydigan odam kerak.»
Sardor ko’zlariga ishonmay turibdi. Boshqa bolalar esa xijolatdan yerga qarab qolibdi.
Shu tariqa Sardor yillar o’tib, mamlakatning adolatli va sevimli podshohi bo’libdi. U har doim aytar ekan: «Halollik bo’sh qo’l bilan kelsa ham, soxta boylikdan qimmat.»

Qissadan hissa: Halollik har doim foyda keltirmaydi, lekin u har doim to’g’ri. Aldab olingan g’alaba kun kelib ochiladi, halol mag’lubiyat esa seni ulug’ qiladi. Haqiqatni aytishdan hech qachon qo’rqma.

quiz.q: All the seeds the king gave had been boiled.
Why did Sardor become the heir?
